text: The live view's shell classification takes a whole command that is a system shell named by its path, /bin/sh, /bin/bash or /bin/zsh, with -c or -lc, as it takes the shell by name: Codex runs every command as /bin/zsh -lc '…', so #226 counted each of Codex's calls as other, with no files. Those three paths are the shells they say on macOS and Linux. Any other path-named command, and any path-named command inside the shell's script, stays other, so the rule of D-0159 holds inside the wrapper. This changes four expectations in #226's acceptance tests, which pinned /bin/sh, /bin/bash and /bin/zsh as other.
